items.title: 1999: A Learjet 35 crashes in Mina near Aberdeen, South Dakota, killing all six people on board, including PGA golfer Payne Stewart and golf course designer Bruce Borland.
items.summary: The Learjet Model 35 and Model 36 are a series of American multi-role business jets and military transport aircraft manufactured by Learjet between 1973 and 1993. When used by the United States Air Force, they carry the designation C-21A. Learjet was acquired by Bombardier Aviation in 1990 as a subsidiary, so the aircraft is also known as the Bombardier Learjet 35.

items.title: 1997: After a civil war, Denis Sassou Nguesso proclaims himself President of the Republic of the Congo.
items.summary: The Second Republic of the Congo Civil War, also known as the Second Brazzaville-Congolese Civil War, was the second of two ethnopolitical civil conflicts in the Republic of the Congo which lasted from 5 June 1997 to 29 December 1999. The war served as the continuation of the civil war of 1993–1994 and involved militias representing three political candidates. The conflict ended following the intervention of the Angolan military, which reinstated former president Denis Sassou Nguesso to power.

items.title: 1995: A commuter train slams into a school bus in Fox River Grove, Illinois, killing seven students.
items.summary: The 1995 Fox River Grove bus–train collision was a grade crossing collision that killed seven students riding aboard a school bus in Fox River Grove, Illinois, on the morning of October 25, 1995. items.title: 1990: The Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic declares its sovereignty from the Soviet Union.
items.summary: The Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic, also known as Soviet Kazakhstan, the Kazakh SSR, KSSR, or simply Kazakhstan, was one of the constituent republics of the Soviet Union (USSR) from 1936 to 1991. Being located in northern Central Asia, the Kazakh SSR was created on 5 December 1936 from the erstwhile Kazakh ASSR, which was an autonomous republic of the Russian SFSR. items.title: 1989: The first leg of the 1989 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira is held at the Estádio da Luz in Lisbon, Portugal.
items.summary: The 1989 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira was the 11th edition of the Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira, the annual Portuguese football season-opening match contested by the winners of the previous season's top league and cup competitions. The 1989 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira was contested over two legs, and opposed Belenenses and Benfica of the Primeira Liga. items.title: 1983: The United States and its Caribbean allies invade Grenada, six days after Prime Minister Maurice Bishop and several of his supporters are executed in a coup d'état.
items.summary: The United States and a coalition of Caribbean countries invaded the island nation of Grenada at dawn on 25 October 1983. It was codenamed Operation Urgent Fury by the U.S. military, and resulted in military occupation within a few days. It was triggered by strife within the People's Revolutionary Government, which led to the house arrest and execution of the previous leader and second Prime Minister of Grenada, Maurice Bishop, and to the establishment of the Revolutionary Military Council…

items.title: 1999: en los Estados Unidos se lanza el microprocesador Pentium III Coppermine, de 733 MHz.
items.summary: El procesador o microprocesador es la unidad de procesamiento principal de un ordenador, es por ello la unidad más importante, el «cerebro» de un ordenador.

items.title: 1999: en Colombia se emite el primer capítulo de Yo soy Betty, la fea, catalogada posteriormente como la telenovela más exitosa de todos los tiempos.
items.summary: Colombia, oficialmente la República de Colombia, es un país soberano situado en la región noroccidental de América del Sur. Se constituye en un Estado unitario, democrático y social de derecho, organizado en 32 departamentos y el distrito Capital de Bogotá. Es el único país de América del Sur con costas tanto en el océano Pacífico como en el océano Atlántico.

items.title: 1997: en Buenos Aires (Argentina) el futbolista Diego Armando Maradona juega el último partido de su carrera profesional.
items.summary: Buenos Aires, históricamente llamada Santa María del Buen Aire, es la capital y ciudad más poblada de Argentina. Sus nombres oficiales son Ciudad de Buenos Aires o Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA). Su denominación previa fue Capital Federal, al declararse sede del Gobierno nacional. Está situada en la región centro-este del país, sobre la orilla sur del Río de la Plata, en la región pampeana. Es uno de los 24 distritos, o «jurisdicciones de primer orden», que conforman el país.

items.title: 1995: en Broadway se estrena el musical Victor/Victoria, protagonizado por Julie Andrews.
items.summary: Broadway es una calle situada en el estado de Nueva York. Broadway empieza junto a State Street en Bowling Green, recorre 21 km a través del borough de Manhattan y 3,2 km a través del Bronx, sale de la ciudad por el norte, recorre otros 29 km por los municipios de Yonkers, Hastings-On-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Irvington y Tarrytown, y termina al norte de Sleepy Hollow, en el condado de Westchester.
